title: Deal Closure to Revenue Onboarding Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the end-to-end operational steps, ownership, and controls required to move a signed customer contract from deal closure through procurement (if applicable), billing, revenue recognition, and incorporation into FP&A forecasts. It reduces handoff risk, ensures audit evidence is collected, and enforces SLAs for revenue and billing accuracy.

Purpose and scope:
- Scope: All commercial contracts (hosted, Dedicated, Private deployments, enterprise add-ons) signed by Sales, Contracting, or Partnerships. Includes subscription, usage, and one-time professional services items.
- Objective: Standardize the path-to-revenue so close date maps to billing and revenue schedules with consistent GL coding, accurate deferred revenue calendars, and clear exception handling.

Key objectives and SLOs:
- Invoice generation: first invoice issued within 7 business days of Contract Execution (target 95% achievement).
- Billing accuracy: initial invoice accuracy rate >= 99.5% (monthly tolerance).
- Revenue posting: deferred revenue schedule loaded to ledger within 3 business days of invoice (target 99%).
- Forecast refresh: FP&A updates committed-revenue and ARR figures within next scheduled weekly close cycle.
- Audit evidence: 100% of enterprise deals have full contract and PII/data-residency checklist attached to the revenue file.

High-level workflow (14 steps):
1) Deal handoff and validation (Sales -> Finance/RevOps/Legal): sales creates a Deal Handoff in CRM with the signed contract PDF, customer billing legal entity, PO (if provided), and approved commercial term sheet. Required fields: contract_id, start_date, billing_frequency, payment_terms, SOW reference.
2) Legal verification (Legal): confirm executed signature blocks, counterparty legal name, and any exceptional clauses (data residency, escrow, KMS). Flag restricted clauses and route to Legal Exceptions.
3) Finance pre-check (RevOps/Finance): review pricing line-items against rate card and discount approvals. Validate product codes map to revenue recognition buckets (subscription, usage, professional services).
4) Procurement setup (Procurement): for customers using PO-based procurement, ensure PO matches contract amount and billing cadence. Create supplier/customer payment terms record where required.
5) Billing enablement (Billing Ops): create billing customer, attach invoice template, set tax, currency, and payment methods. Create initial invoice schedule in billing system.
6) Invoice generation & validation (Billing Ops -> Sales): generate the first invoice and send to customer. Sales confirms receipt and PO mapping if applicable.
7) Deferred revenue schedule creation (Accounting): create deferred revenue schedule CSV and attach to month close packet. Include contract_id, invoice_id, start_date, end_date, recognition_method, total_amount, monthly_amount.
8) Journal entry & GL mapping (Accounting): post deferred revenue/initial invoice entries. See sample entry below.
9) Forecast & FP&A ingestion (FP&A): import committed ARR and expected cash timing into forecast and update booking pipeline. Change flags for timing risk.
10) Collections follow-up (AR): monitor receivables and escalate according to Collections SOP.
11) Monthly recognition review (Accounting & Product Finance): reconcile usage or variable components and adjust recognition run- rate.
12) Contract amendments & renewals (Sales -> RevOps): process amendments through the same pipeline; tag as amendment and link to original contract_id.
13) Audit evidence bundle (Accounting): compile contract, invoice, PO, billing communications, and revenue schedule into the deal folder.
14) Close loop & metrics (RevOps): surface exceptions to Sales Ops for quota/cross-team follow-up.

Approval and signature matrix (top-level):
| Contract value (USD) | Required approvals | Legal SLA | Finance SLA | Procurement involvement |
|----------------------:|--------------------|----------:|-----------:|------------------------:|
| < 50k                | AE / Sales Manager | 2 business days | 2 business days | No unless PO required |
| 50k - 250k           | AE / Sales Manager / Sales Director | 3 business days | 3 business days | Optional PO setup |
| > 250k               | AE / Sales Dir / VP Sales / Legal Counsel | 5 business days | 5 business days | Procurement required for POs |

Roles & ownership (contact list):
- Sales: deal documentation, customer contact, escalation for billing disputes. Primary contact: Sales AE.
- Legal: contract execution confirmation, clause exceptions, negotiation support. Owner: Legal Counsel (Commercial).
- RevOps: deal ingestion into systems, CRM mappings, subscription/product code mapping. Owner: RevOps Manager.
- Billing Ops: invoice generation and delivery, tax & remittance config. Owner: Billing Lead.
- Accounting: deferred revenue schedules, journal entries, month-end recognition. Owner: Accounting Manager.
- FP&A: incorporate bookings into forecast and variance analysis. Owner: FP&A Director.
- Procurement: validate PO-based collections and vendor setup for services. Owner: Head of Procurement.

Required artifacts (checklist per enterprise deal):
- Signed contract (PDF) with execution date and valid signature blocks.
- Approved commercial term sheet or quote.
- Customer billing legal entity & tax ID.
- PO (if applicable) matching contract lines.
- Billing contact and remit-to email/address.
- SOW (for professional services) with milestones and acceptance criteria.
- Data-residency and KMS confirmation where relevant.
- Pricing and discount approval evidence.
- First invoice and payment confirmation (or notes if delayed).

Exception handling (common scenarios):
- Missing PO: create temporary billing hold and flag procurement; issue invoice when PO is provided, capture communication for audit.
- Disputed invoice: escalate to Billing Ops with detailed dispute reason; Sales to coordinate with customer; avoid recognizing disputed revenue until resolved if collectibility is materially in question.
- Amendments to subscription term: treat as contract modification per RevRec policy; map delta to the original performance obligation and remeasure remaining revenue.

Example journal entries (monthly, simplified):
- When invoice issued for annual prepaid subscription USD 120,000 on 2025-03-01 (recognize monthly over 12 months):
```
DR Accounts Receivable 120,000
  CR Unearned Revenue (deferred) 120,000
```
- Monthly recognition (first month 2025-03-31):
```
DR Unearned Revenue 10,000
  CR Subscription Revenue 10,000
```
- One-time professional services recognized on delivery (USD 30,000):
```
DR Accounts Receivable 30,000
  CR Professional Services Revenue 30,000
```

Mapping of line items to recognition buckets (examples):
- Product: Subscription (time-based) -> recognized ratably over term.
- Usage: Variable -> recognized as invoiced or measured (monthly) with estimate/true-up.
- Professional services: Point-in-time -> recognized on delivery/acceptance.

Revenue forecasting integration rules (FP&A):
- Committed ARR: convert signed subscription ARR to ARR metric at contract effective date; exclude services.
- Cash timing: use invoice payment terms and historical collection rates; apply DSO assumptions for the forecast bucket.
- Adjustments: late PO flag or negotiation hold reduces near-term recognized revenue until resolution. Document all manual overrides with an approver and rationale.

Controls and audit evidence requirements:
- Every posted deferred revenue schedule must reference a contract_id and have a signer (Accounting).
- Maintain a single source of truth for contract metadata in CRM; RevOps is responsible for reconciliation weekly.
- Retain evidence for 7 years for audit (contract, PO, invoice, acceptance).
- Random monthly sample: internal audit will review 5% of enterprise deals for completeness and accuracy.

Operational runbook excerpts (day-to-day):
- Billing Ops day 0: ingest deal, verify tax jurisdiction, create invoice schedule.
- Accounting day 1-3: create deferred schedule, post journal stub.
- FP&A weekly: run committed ARR upload and reconcile with CRM bookings.
- AR days 15-30: monitor collections and initiate second-level escalation for >30 days overdue.

Common templates (links and inline examples):
- Deferred revenue schedule CSV header: contract_id,invoice_id,start_date,end_date,total_amount,recognition_period_months,monthly_amount,account_code
- Contract attachment naming convention: <customer>-<contract_id>-signed.pdf
- Email subject template to customer when sending invoice: "Invoice [invoice_id] for [customer] — [period start] to [period end]"

Metrics and reporting (weekly/monthly):
- Weekly: # deals ingested, # invoices generated within SLA, exceptions open.
- Monthly: Revenue recognized vs. bookings, billing accuracy %, DSO, deferred revenue roll-forward.

Onboarding items for new systems or tool changes:
- If billing provider changes, Billing Ops must provide a 6-week migration runbook: parallel invoicing, reconciliation plan, rollback window, and test customers.
- RevOps must run a contract metadata export and reconcile field mappings before cutover.

Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: When do we treat a license change as a new contract vs amendment?
A: If the change affects the term or introduces new performance obligations that change the economics materially (>10% value change), it should be a contract amendment and follow amendment rules. Small line-item adjustments can be amendments but must be tagged and remeasured.

Q: What documentation proves collectibility?
A: Signed contract, PO (if applicable), evidence of billing communication, historical payment behavior, and credit review. If collectibility is uncertain, revenue recognition is deferred pending resolution.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for deal intake (copy-pasteable):
- [ ] Signed contract attached (PDF)
- [ ] Commercial term sheet uploaded
- [ ] Customer billing legal entity & tax ID recorded
- [ ] PO attached or procurement note added
- [ ] Invoice contact and remit address provided
- [ ] SOW or services acceptance criteria attached (if applicable)
- [ ] Pricing approver evidence attached
- [ ] Data residency/KMS flags noted (if applicable)

Appendix B — Escalation contacts:
- Billing disputes (Billing Ops): billing-ops@redwood.ai
- Contract/legal exceptions (Legal): legal-commercial@redwood.ai
- RevRec policy questions (Accounting): accounting@redwood.ai
- FP&A forecast queries (FP&A): fpand a@redwood.ai
